facts.statement: Before asking anything, ground in context — scan the environment for patterns, integration points, and unstated constraints; never ask a question the codebase already answers — then restate the interpretation in natural language with assumptions explicit before drafting
Interview with a single focused question per turn until every Spec field is answered; never batch questions into one message; ask clarifying questions rather than writing a plan document

The Spec block has exactly nine fields — Goal, In scope, Out of scope, Assumptions, Success criteria, Output format, Audience, Grounding context, Failure cases; skip a field only when the user explicitly waives it

Once every Spec field has an answer — whether elicited one question at a time or supplied up front by the user — present the filled Spec block and ask the user to confirm or correct it; never draft the prompt in the same turn as the spec
On confirmation, write the complete prompt text in a single code fence encoding every Spec field; the deliverable is the prompt artifact itself — do not execute the task the prompt describes
Keep the prompt model-agnostic: omit few-shot exemplars, chain-of-thought scaffolding, and role personas; add a prompting technique only when the user explicitly requests it

Iron Law: no drafts before sign-off — no exceptions; a deadline, deploy window, 'we'll fix it later,' or a demand to 'just draft something' does not waive the interview, and the compliant response to resistance is exactly the standard one: restate the interpretation and ask the single most important open question; listing assumptions at the top of a draft is still a draft — a field is answered only when the user has confirmed or corrected it

Do not shape when the request is already specific (names files, behavior, success criteria) — draft the prompt directly; when it is purely informational — nothing to scope; when the user already corrected a previous interpretation — apply the correction, don't re-interview; a request to skip the interview, a deadline, impatience, or 'we'll fix it later' is a complaint about process, not a correction of interpretation, and does not waive the interview or permit drafting early

excluded.reason: frontmatter-convention guidance is always out of scope
